clue.text: Such a man could not be classed capital fellow.

definitions.text: Such a man could not be classed capital fellow.

parts.words: Such a man could not be classed capital fellow.
parts.note: capital fellow reads as praise for a splendid chap, but means a man from the capital city, which this person is not

explanation.surface: Someone is judged not quite a splendid chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the regions, away from the metropolis, is by definition not a man of the capital.

clue.text: Is it a support to the poor actor?

definitions.text: Is it a support to the poor actor?

parts.words: Is it a support to the poor actor?
parts.note: a support in the general sense, and also the stage object an actor handles, which helps a weak performer along

explanation.surface: Asking whether a struggling performer gets any help.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage property is shortened in theatre slang, and the same word means a support or brace.

clue.text: Coal-pit's purely visual outcome.

indicators.note: the outcome of the coal-pit is what its letters turn into once rearranged

parts.note: the letters of coal-pit, the possessive adding none

explanation.surface: A mine produces something that is only a matter of appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outcome' signals rearranging the letters of COAL-PIT; the possessive 's gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relating only to sight or seeing, an illusion for example, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Man of morals providing a pose of sorts.

indicators.note: a pose of sorts is a loose version of the phrase a pose, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An ethical man strikes some kind of attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of sorts' signals rearranging the letters of A POSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek fabulist ended each of his animal tales with a moral, so he is a teller of morals.

clue.text: The last to be seen of the hare?

definitions.text: The last to be seen of the hare?

parts.words: The last to be seen of the hare?
parts.note: as a hare runs off, the final thing visible is its short white tail

explanation.surface: Wondering what one last glimpses of a fleeing hare.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name for the short erect tail of a hare, rabbit or deer.

clue.text: "Heaven's cherubim, hors'd Upon the sightless ___s of the air." (Macbeth.)

definitions.text: "Heaven's cherubim, hors'd Upon the sightless ___s of the air." (Macbeth.)

parts.words: "Heaven's cherubim, hors'd Upon the sightless ___s of the air." (Macbeth.)
parts.note: a quotation from Macbeth's speech before the murder of Duncan, with one word blanked out: the invisible winds are pictured as messengers on which the cherubim ride

explanation.surface: A line of Shakespeare with a gap to fill.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is a messenger, the winds being imagined as swift carriers of news.

clue.text: Writing about a place ? Exactly.

parts.note: the Greek roots of the word are literally place plus writing, so the description fits exactly

explanation.surface: Someone describes a location and is told that is precisely right.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek elements topos, a place, and graphein, to write, combine to mean the description of a region's features.

clue.text: This means the end of one's best suit

definitions.text: This means the end of one's best suit

parts.words: This means the end of one's best suit
parts.note: in card play the final card of the trump suit, the strongest suit, ends it; the phrase is also the call ending the world at the Judgment

explanation.surface: Someone's finest set of clothes has worn out at last.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpet sounding on Judgment Day signals the end of everything, while at cards the final trump ends that suit.

clue.text: The way a ghost is seen through ?

definitions.text: The way a ghost is seen through ?

parts.words: The way a ghost is seen through ?
parts.note: a ghost is see-through, and to be seen through also means to have one's pretence detected easily

explanation.surface: Describing how a phantom appears to onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is pictured as see-through, and an obvious deceiver is seen through clearly, so both senses of the adverb apply.

clue.text: A number of simultaneous discharges — most dangerous!

definitions.text: A number of simultaneous discharges — most dangerous!

parts.words: A number of simultaneous discharges — most dangerous!
parts.note: a warship firing all the guns on one side at once delivers a volley of this kind, plainly the most perilous thing to face

explanation.surface: Several guns go off at once, to deadly effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Firing every gun along a ship's flank together is the naval term, and the plural covers several such volleys.

clue.text: That post-siege feeling.

parts.note: a besieged town freed by outside forces has had its siege lifted, and its people feel freed from anxiety

explanation.surface: The mood once a long blockade is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison whose siege is lifted is said to be freed in this way, and the same word means feeling eased after worry.

clue.text: Tasty type-to be found 'in a store.

indicators.note: being found jumbled within the phrase a store means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something delicious can be bought in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be found in' signals rearranging the letters of A STORE. 'Tasty type' is a jokey definition for the edible oyster's genus name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Latin genus name of the true oysters, a delicacy, so a tasty kind of shellfish.

clue.text: Alarming beast this was to nomads perhaps.

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the phrase to nomads is to be taken loosely, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: A frightening animal that wandering tribesmen once feared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals rearranging the letters of TO NOMADS.
explanation.definitionFit: This extinct elephant-like creature with great tusks would have been an alarming animal to early peoples.

clue.text: One way to form a tie.

definitions.text: One way to form a tie.

parts.words: One way to form a tie.
parts.note: a tie sounds like a necktie or a drawn game, but here it is a bond or link made by fastening

explanation.definitionFit: To fasten or join one thing to another is to create a bond between them.

clue.text: Proverbially a man for an oath.

definitions.text: Proverbially a man for an oath.

parts.words: Proverbially a man for an oath.
parts.note: the saying swear like a cavalry soldier makes him the proverbial curser

explanation.surface: Describing a man famous for swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase to swear like a cavalry private makes him proverbial for bad language.

clue.text: Refrain from the song of Queen Mab's tainted attendant.

indicators.note: the answer is drawn out from within the words that follow, spanning two of them

explanation.surface: Holding back from the song of Queen Mab's corrupt fairy servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals taking the letters out of the run MAB'S TAINTED. Queen Mab is the fairy queen of English folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back or decline to indulge is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Trump call that may dwindle away.

definitions.meaning: in bridge or whist, playing a high card before a low one is a signal asking partner to lead trumps
the verb, usually with out, means to fade gradually to nothing

explanation.definitionFit: In whist the signal for trumps has this name, and to fade gradually is to do this out.

clue.text: The cheek of a fellow!

definitions.meaning: an old word for the jaw or cheek, usually plural

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old term for the jaw or cheek, as in chops, and informal British for a man.

clue.text: "Who steals my purse steals" (Othello.)

parts.note: Iago's line in Othello, the next word saying that money is worthless rubbish compared with a good name

explanation.surface: A line of Shakespeare waiting to be completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago calls a stolen purse worthless rubbish, beside the loss of one's good name.

clue.text: Wounded return of the young archer.

indicators.note: the name of the archer god comes back, so it is read in the other direction

parts.note: Eros, the Greek god of love, is pictured as a boy with bow and arrows

explanation.surface: Someone is hurt as the youthful bowman comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful or injured part of the body can be described with this adjective.

clue.text: Forty winks brought on by a ginger biscuit

definitions.text: Forty winks brought on by a ginger biscuit

parts.words: Forty winks brought on by a ginger biscuit
parts.note: forty winks is a nap, and the nap a spirit brings on gives a spirit's nap, which also names a ginger biscuit

explanation.surface: Dozing off after eating a ginger biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: This rolled crisp wafer flavoured with ginger is a classic British teatime biscuit, its name splitting into a liquor plus a doze.
